title: List failed system services and read why one failed
summary: Show the systemd services that failed to start or crashed, then read the last log lines of one of them to find the reason it broke.
prerequisites: Linux that uses systemd (Ubuntu, Mint, Debian, Fedora, Arch)

steps.explain: List the services (units) that systemd marked as failed. Look at the ACTIVE and SUB columns: 'failed' means the unit stopped because of an error. The last line shows how many units failed.
steps.expect: A table with UNIT, LOAD, ACTIVE and SUB columns and a final count such as '1 loaded units listed.', or '0 loaded units listed.' if nothing failed.

alternatives.explain: Show the status of all units that are currently in a failed state.
alternatives.expect: A list of failed units, or a message indicating no failed units were found.

steps.explain: Show the status of one failed service. Replace <UNIT_NAME> with a name from the first list, for example cups.service. Look at the 'Active:' line and the last log lines at the bottom of the output.

placeholders.name: UNIT_NAME
placeholders.description: Name of a failed service from the list (the .service suffix is optional)

steps.expect: A header with the service name and an 'Active:' line that says 'failed' with a Result such as 'exit-code', followed by the last few log lines.

steps.explain: Show the last 50 log lines of that service, oldest first. The error message near the end usually says why it failed, for example a missing file or a port that is already in use.

placeholders.name: UNIT_NAME
placeholders.description: Same failed service name as in the previous step

steps.expect: Up to 50 log lines of the service, oldest first. The error line near the end gives the reason; if the list is empty or very short, try the alternative.

alternatives.explain: Use this if the output is empty or misses lines. The system log can need administrator rights to read, so run the same command with sudo and type your password.

placeholders.name: UNIT_NAME
placeholders.description: Same failed service name as in the previous step

alternatives.expect: The same kind of log lines, now including messages that were hidden without sudo.
